questions.question: State the general formula for alkanes and give the molecular formula of the alkane with 8 carbon atoms.
Explain why the combustion of methane produces a higher amount of heat energy per mole of carbon compared to the combustion of ethane.
Describe the initiation step in a free‑radical substitution reaction of chloromethane with a hydrogen atom.
A sample of 2‑bromopropane is reacted with sodium hydroxide in ethanol. State the type of substitution reaction that occurs and write the product.
Compare the relative rates of hydrolysis for 1‑bromobutane and 1‑chlorobutane and explain the reason for any difference.
A 0.10 M solution of 1‑chlorobutane is reacted with 0.20 M NaOH in ethanol. Calculate the concentration of the alkoxide ion after 5 min if the rate constant for the substitution reaction is 0.02 s⁻¹.
State the general rule for the addition of hydrogen bromide to an alkene.
Explain the mechanism of the electrophilic addition of HCl to propene, including the role of the carbocation intermediate.
A polymerisation reaction of ethene using a radical initiator produces polyethylene. Describe the propagation step of this polymerisation.
A laboratory experiment shows that the addition of H₂O₂ to 1‑hexene gives a mixture of alcohols. Explain why the product distribution is not a single compound.
